dial.summary: 10Y Treasury retreating from its 5.35% cycle high to 5.24% may signal the beginning of a yield peak, but DXY at 102.25 and real yields at 2.92% keep macro headwinds in place; BTC.D firm at 58.5% and perp funding near 0.0067% confirm spot-led accumulation remains intact, with October 14 CPI the dominant catalyst for the next macro regime shift.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.6T based on StreetStats/MacroMicro snapshot as of August 2026 ($103,649B–$103,663B); most recent month with all four central banks reporting is August 2026 (6–8 week reporting lag); 4-week trend flat: no confirmed September G4 data available; 3-month constant-FX G4 change +0.87% (significantly below historical average); YoY still positive (not contracting); status neutral — confirmed rising 4-week trend required for supportive; next G4 M2 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI = 54.5%, released October 1, 2026 (most recent release; next release November 2, 2026 for October data); 4-week trend flat: August 54.6% → September 54.5% = −0.1pp, within flat threshold; New Orders 55.3% (+1.6pp), Production 56.7% (−1.6pp), Prices 77.9% (highest since mid-2021), Backlogs 56.4% (+4.6pp); status neutral (above 50 but not rising on 4-week basis — supportive requires both above 50 AND rising); manufacturing sector expanded for ninth consecutive month in September.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot at 102.25 (October 8, 2026 close; Investing.com historical table; Dealplexus confirms 102.22 close Oct 8, 52-week high 102.54 set Oct 5); 4-week trend up: ~99.9 (Sep 5) → 102.25 (Oct 8) = +2.35% over 30 days; status headwind (above 100 threshold); note: 10Y Treasury eased to 5.23–5.24% on Oct 8–9 from 5.35% peak, may signal early DXY softening — a sustained close below 100 required for neutral status; October 14 CPI is the next major DXY repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.92% as of October 7, 2026 (Federal Reserve H.15 confirmed; Oct 5: 2.95%, Oct 6: 2.91%, Oct 7: 2.92%; StreetStats Oct 8: 2.91%); 4-week trend up: ~2.50% (Sep 3) → 2.92% (Oct 7) = +42bps; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% threshold both met); 10Y yield easing from 5.35% peak to 5.23% on Oct 9 could moderate real yields — October 14 CPI is the key repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 8, 2026: 10Y Treasury at 5.24% (Forbes/StreetStats Oct 8 close), 2Y at 4.77% → 2s10s spread = +0.47% (+47bps); spread narrowed from +55bps intraday peak on Oct 7 as long-end yields retreated from 5.35% cycle high; 4-week trend up (steepening on 4-week basis): Sep 5 spread ~+42bps → Oct 8 +47bps = +5bps steepening over 30 days; status supportive (positive and steepening on 4-week basis — both criteria met); October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are the next major yield curve catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,747,560M ($6.748T) for week ending October 7, 2026 (Federal Reserve H.4.1 released October 8, 2026; FRED confirmed); prior readings: Sep 30 $6,743,031M, Sep 23 $6,747,704M; 4-week trend flat: Sep 9 ~$6,737M → Oct 7 $6,748M = +$11B (+0.16%), marginal expansion within flat threshold on a $6.75T base; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no QT acceleration); next H.4.1 release October 15, 2026 covering week ending October 14.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately 0.0067% per 8h (MacroMicro as of September 30, 2026; prior reading 0.0066%); no confirmed October data available at time of this run (6–8 hour settlement cycles mean rates update continuously); 4-week trend up: ~0.003% per 8h (early Sep) → 0.0067% (Sep 30) = rising but well-controlled; status supportive (0.0067% well below 0.04% overheating threshold — confirms spot-driven accumulation, not leveraged speculation); October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are next potential funding regime shift catalysts.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$307B (DefiLlama early October 2026); total crypto market cap ~$2.9T (Oct 1–8 aggregators: $2.87T–$2.92T); stablecoin dominance ~10.6% (arithmetic: $307B / $2.9T); BTC.D 58.5% (tv-hub.org Oct 2026); 30-day trend flat: ~10.4% (Sep 5) → ~10.6% (Oct 8) = marginal change within flat threshold; status neutral (not falling on 30-day basis = not supportive; TOTAL rising but stablecoin share also marginally rising = headwind condition not confirmed); ~$307B sidelined capital available to deploy if macro improves; October 14 CPI is the next stablecoin inflow/outflow catalyst.

upcoming.title: CPI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — the dominant macro catalyst before the October 27–28 FOMC decision; August CPI YoY was +3.4–3.5%; ISM Manufacturing Prices at 77.9% (highest since mid-2021) is a leading upside signal; a hot print above +3.5% YoY could revive October hike odds, push DXY above 104, and reverse the recent yield retreat; a dovish miss below +3.0% YoY would cement Fed hold expectations, catalyze DXY below 100, and potentially trigger a BTC breakout above $90K; real yields at 2.92% and DXY at 102.25 make this the single most important data point of the month.

upcoming.title: PPI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — pipeline inflation released the day after CPI; August PPI Final Demand was +2.8% YoY; ISM Manufacturing Prices at 77.9% is a leading signal for potential PPI upside; a hot PPI following a hot CPI would reinforce October hike expectations and likely drive DXY back above 103; released alongside Retail Sales and Initial Jobless Claims, making October 15 the most data-dense morning before the October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Retail Sales for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released alongside September PPI and Initial Jobless Claims; given the September NFP shock (+29K), a weak retail sales print would confirm broad economic softening and reinforce Fed hold narrative; a strong print alongside weak labor extends the late-cycle bifurcation signal (resilient consumer, softening employment); provides key pre-FOMC context on Q3 consumer demand ahead of the October 29 GDP advance estimate.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 11, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended October 11, 2026 — second consecutive weekly claims read post the September NFP shock (+29K); released alongside PPI and Retail Sales, making October 15 the most data-dense pre-FOMC morning; a second consecutive above-200K print would confirm labor market softening is a trend; claims trajectory directly informs market odds for a Fed pause vs. hike at the October 27–28 meeting.

upcoming.title: Fed Balance Sheet H.4.1 (week ended October 14, 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve H.4.1 weekly balance sheet release at 4:30 PM ET — covers week ending October 14, 2026; prior reading $6,747,560M ($6.748T, week ending Oct 7); four consecutive weeks of flat-to-marginal expansion; a shift toward contraction combined with rising overnight rates would flip status from supportive to headwind; flat or marginally expanding expected given recent stabilization trend.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production & Capacity Utilization (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Board releases September 2026 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization at 9:15 AM ET; completes the Q3 output picture ahead of GDP advance estimate (October 29); September ISM Manufacturing at 54.5% and Production Index at 56.7% suggest solid output growth; capacity utilization near 78–79% would be consistent with expansion without excess inflationary pressure; a miss alongside the September NFP shock would reinforce the stagflation (hot prices, softening activity) narrative into the October 27–28 FOMC.
